name: Mariam-uz-Zamani
role: Empress Consort of Mughal Emperor Akbar
contribution: The Chief consort and favourite wife of the third Mughal emperor, Akbar, and the mother of his successor, Jahangir.
legacy: She was among the few Mughal women granted the exceptional privilege of issuing imperial farmans in her own name, and was the first recorded Mughal woman to engage in overseas trade through her merchant fleets, which also transported Hajj pilgrims to Mecca.

checks.lead: Mariam-uz-Zamani (lit. 'Mary/Compassionate of the Age'; 1543 – 19 May 1623) was the Chief consort and favourite wife of the third Mughal emperor, Akbar, and the mother of his successor, Jahangir. She was Akbar's most influential wife and the longest-serving Hindu empress in the Mughal Empire, for forty-three years.
